newsitem.title: USA: Late NYMEX Hub natgas holds short covering gains.
newsitem.headline: Late NYMEX Hub natgas holds short covering gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures, defying early reports of softer physical prices, held modest gains late Friday in sluggish trade, still bolstered by some pre-weekend shortcovering, industry sources said.
At 1445 EDT, June gained 4.5 cents to $2.24 per million British thermal units, while July was six cents higher at $2.26. Most other deferreds were up one to 4.5 cents.
"There's a little shortcovering, but I think the fundamentals dictate a near-term pullback. We're not going to have any load next week in the Midwest or Northeast," said one East Coast trader.
But opinions differed on the potential effect of next week's forecasts, with some expecting steady injection demand and some heat in Texas and the South to prop up the cash.
Technically, traders pegged June support in the $2.15 area, with major buying expected at $2.05. Key resistance was seen at $2.30 and then at the contract high of $2.43.

In the cash, Gulf Coast weekend prices slipped a nickel to the mid-to-high teens. Midcon pipes were off more than five cents to the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas also lost some ground to the low-to-mid $2.40s.
Maintenance on Transco's Texas line, which began Saturday, will continue to cut the line's total capacity of about 600 mmcfd through Monday, with 400 mmcfd still cut May 20-22.
NYMEX said 24,370 contracts traded by 1410 EDT.
On KCBT, June climbed 4.2 cents to $2.10, while deferreds were steady to five cents higher. The East/West spread widened by 0.3 cent to 14.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
